newsitem.title: UK: Guinness board does not comment on merger.
newsitem.headline: Guinness board does not comment on merger.

text.p: A regular board meeting of drinks group Guinness Plc on Wednesday ended without any comment on its proposed merger with Grand Metropolitan or alternative proposals from Bernard Arnault, chairman of French company LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton.

There had been speculation in the media that an announcement might be made on the proposals from LMVH, which are aimed at scuppering the 24 billion stg merger plan and creating a three-way drinks combination.
Arnault's resignation from the Guinness board, made earlier this week, was accepted by the board meeting, because of his "conflict of interest."
The two British firms are expected to deliver a response to Arnault's plans later this week or possibly next, observers said on Wednesday.
Guinness said no deadline had been set for any announcement.

"Both Grand Metropolitan and ourselves are still working on a very detailed response to M. Arnault's proposals. No deadline has been set for completion of the document. A response will be delivered to M. Arnault when it is ready and not before," a Guinness spokesman said.

LMVH has increased its stake in GrandMet to 11.05 percent from 6.4 percent and brought its holding in Guinness down to 12.46 percent from 14.2 percent in frenzied turnover on the London stock market on Tuesday.
Arnault was seen attempting to gain leverage through his stakes to push his proposals against the merger plan of the two British firms.
